task: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Carvana

merged.claim: Carvana Co. (NYSE: CVNA) is a public, Garcia-family-controlled company with dual-class shares. Ernie Garcia III is Chairman and CEO. Ernest Garcia II is the largest individual shareholder and controls related companies DriveTime and Bridgecrest. There is no PE sponsor and no recent change of control.
The Garcia family holds about 83% of voting power (Dec 31, 2025, per the 10-K and Fitch). The 2026 proxy says the Garcia Parties keep 10 votes per Class B share while meeting the ownership condition.
The Garcia family controls roughly 85% of voting power via super-voting Class B shares; Ernest Garcia II holds about a 7% economic stake.
Q2 2026 (three months ended 2026-06-30) net sales and operating revenues were $7.376 billion, up 52% YoY.
Revenue for the six months ended 2026-06-30 was $13.808 billion.
LTM revenue for the period ended 2026-06-30 was $25.058 billion.
LTM operating income for the period ended 2026-06-30 was $2.237 billion.
Q2 2026 GAAP operating income was $680 million.
Q2 2026 GAAP net income was $513 million (7.0% margin, a quarterly record).
Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was $769 million (10.4% margin, a record).
Full-year 2025 Adjusted EBITDA was $2.240 billion.
On 2026-07-29 Carvana issued FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.7-$3.0 billion.
Cash and cash equivalents were $2.630 billion at 2026-06-30.
Restricted cash was $113 million at 2026-06-30, separate from cash and cash equivalents.
Total debt (Note 9, excluding finance leases) was $5.133 billion at 2026-06-30.
Finance lease liabilities were $118 million at 2026-06-30, separate from Note 9 debt.
The tax receivable agreement liability was $2.130 billion at 2026-06-30, separate from debt.
Total liabilities were $9.414 billion at 2026-06-30.
Current debt principal (excluding finance leases) was $319 million at 2026-06-30.
$32 million of unsecured notes are due April 15, 2027.
Net cash provided by operating activities was $345 million for the six months ended 2026-06-30.
Availability under revolving facilities, based on pledgeable assets, was $2.039 billion at 2026-06-30.
Committed liquidity resources, including cash, were $4.669 billion at 2026-06-30.
Total liquidity resources were $7.024 billion at 2026-06-30, including conditional additional debt capacity and unpledged securities.

In Q2 2026 (May) Carvana added a new $500 million revolving finance-receivable facility (the seventh) available through November 8, 2027. Finance-receivable facilities had zero drawn and $4.1 billion of unused capacity at 2026-06-30, though collateral-based immediately available borrowing is lower.
A March 2026 amendment increased another finance-receivable facility to $600 million and extended its maturity to June 30, 2027.

On 2026-07-27 Carvana amended its Ally Master Purchase and Sale Agreement, raising Ally's commitment to buy finance-receivable principal to up to $8.0 billion from July 27, 2026 through July 26, 2027.
Management expects working capital, operating cash flow and continued or new financing to fund operations for at least one year from issuance of the Q2 2026 10-Q (conditional guidance).
Carvana reported compliance with all debt covenants at 2026-06-30, and the 10-Q item 'Defaults Upon Senior Securities' was None.

On 2026-08-14 Carvana entered a $1.66 billion senior secured Term Loan B due 2033-08-14. It was issued at 99.75 and priced at Term SOFR+2.25% (base rate+1.25%), with 0.25% quarterly amortization and a 50% excess cash flow sweep from FY2028. It is guaranteed by material domestic subsidiaries, secured by substantially all collateral, and has no financial covenant. Proceeds refinance the 2030 secured notes; this is a refinancing, not a distressed exchange.
Carvana redeemed its 9.0%/11.0%/13.0% Cash/PIK Senior Secured Notes due 2030 using Term Loan B proceeds: $1.0 billion on 2026-08-15 and the remainder on 2026-08-22.

Management estimated on 2026-08-12 that the Term Loan B refinancing would cut annual cash interest by about $45 million over the next four years on a leverage-neutral basis (a company estimate, not realized savings).

In August 2023 Carvana launched an out-of-court distressed exchange of 5.500% 2027, 5.875% 2028, 4.875% 2029 and 10.250% 2030 unsecured notes for up to $4.275 billion of new Cash/PIK senior secured notes due 2028/2030/2031. Holders of more than 90% committed, and the exchange completed in September 2023. Fitch cites it as part of the credit history.
In August 2023 Carvana launched a $425.0 million cash tender offer for its 5.625% 2025 notes at 85% of par, with covenant-stripping consent solicitations.

Carvana moved to fully cash-paying interest in August 2025, and a $1.26 billion equity offering partly funded voluntary debt reduction. Unrestricted cash was about $1.86 billion at 2025-06-30, and debt/EBITDA was about 3.2x for the LTM to 2025-06-30.
Carvana recorded about $320 million of non-cash PIK interest in the period ended 2025-06-30.
Carvana has a $1 billion at-the-market equity facility, after raising $1.3 billion via ATM in 2024 and redeeming $470 million of 2028 senior secured notes in 2024.
On 2026-07-30 Fitch assigned Carvana a first-time Long-Term IDR of BB- with Stable Outlook (secured notes BB+/RR2, unsecured notes BB-/RR4).
Fitch (2026-07-30) noted that customer-loan sales represented 56% of 2025 EBITDA and that access to securitization/loan buyers is important to liquidity.
Fitch (2026-07-30) flagged Carvana's controlled-company status and related-party transactions as a structural credit risk.
On 2026-03-03 S&P affirmed Carvana's issuer credit rating at BB- with Positive outlook, upgraded the senior secured issue rating to BB from BB-, and affirmed the senior unsecured rating at B.
On 2026-08-05 S&P affirmed Carvana's BB- issuer credit rating with a positive outlook and rated the proposed $1.0 billion senior secured term loan BB with Recovery Rating 2.
On 2025-03-14 S&P upgraded Carvana to 'B' from 'B-' (senior secured B, senior unsecured CCC+) with positive outlook; a further upgrade is possible if leverage stays below 5x and FOCF/debt above 5%.
On 2026-06-24 Moody's upgraded Carvana's long-term rating to B1 from B2 with Positive outlook (as reported by Cbonds).
On 2026-07-01 Moody's upgraded Carvana's long-term rating to B1 from B2 and assigned a positive outlook.
On 2026-10-08 Moody's assigned a B1 rating to Carvana's $1.66 billion senior secured term loan; the CFR remained B1 with positive outlook.
On 2025-10-02 Moody's upgraded Carvana's CFR to B2 from B3 with positive outlook (senior secured B2 from B3, senior unsecured Caa1 from Caa2).

Moody's (Oct 2025) cited about $985M of LTM gains on receivable sales and debt/EBITDA of about 3.2x. It said good liquidity depends on continued ability to sell receivables at significant gains, and that a further upgrade needs debt/EBITDA below 4.0x and EBITDA-capex/interest above 3.0x.
On 2025-03-27 Moody's upgraded Carvana's CFR to B3 from Caa1 (PDR B3-PD, SGL-2) with positive outlook; debt/EBITDA improved to about 4.2x at FYE2024 from about 18.8x at FYE2023.

On 2026-01-28 short seller Gotham City Research accused Carvana of overstating 2023-2024 earnings by more than $1 billion and of undisclosed dependence on related parties DriveTime and Bridgecrest. CVNA fell 14.2% to $410.04, and Carvana called the report inaccurate and misleading.
On 2026-02-20 CFO Mark Jenkins called the short-seller related-party allegations '100% inaccurate' on the Q4 2025 earnings call; no CFO departure or auditor change was reported.
Hindenburg Research disclosed a short position in Carvana on 2025-01-02, calling the turnaround a 'mirage' propped up by unstable loans and accounting manipulation.
Carvana cut about 2,500 employees (~12% of workforce) in 2022 and a further ~1,500 (~8%) in November 2022 as used-car sales fell.

On 2025-01-14 the Connecticut Attorney General announced a $1.5 million settlement with Carvana over title/registration delays, delayed seller payments, delayed loan payoffs and condition misrepresentations: $1 million restitution plus a $500,000 penalty ($250,000 suspended on compliance). The investigation began January 2022 and the settlement is subject to court approval.
The accrual for unresolved legal matters was $10 million at 2026-06-30, versus $14 million at December 31, 2025.
Grant Thornton LLP (auditor since 2015) issued an unqualified opinion on the 2025 financial statements and effective internal control over financial reporting, with no going-concern qualification.
Carvana scheduled Q3 2026 results for October 28, 2026, so the latest quarterly financials available are for June 30, 2026.

c1.note: Carvana is public (NYSE: CVNA) with dual-class shares and Garcia family control. There is no PE sponsor. I could not open the cited Fitch page, and I did not confirm the DriveTime and Bridgecrest link.

c2.note: The May 2026 8-K vote counts put Class B at about 83% of total votes, and the 10-vote-per-share mechanism is confirmed. The Fitch and 10-K pages could not be opened, so the 'Garcia family' attribution is inferred.

c3.note: Only a search summary of the secondary source shows about 85% voting power and about 7% economic stake. The page would not load, and the 85% differs slightly from the roughly 83% from the 8-K.

c4.note: Q2 2026 total revenue was $7.376B, up 52% YoY, per search results on the release. I did not open the release itself.

c5.note: Q1 revenue of $6.432B plus Q2 revenue of $7.376B equals $13.808B. The cited stocktitan page returned 404.

c6.note: I did not read the LTM figure directly. Q1'26 ($6.432B) plus Q2'26 ($7.376B) leave $11.25B for Q3 and Q4 2025, which fits roughly $5.65B per quarter, so $25.058B is consistent.

c7.note: Q3'25 $552M + Q4'25 $424M + Q1'26 $581M + Q2'26 $680M = $2,237M. Q1'26 and Q2'26 come from company releases. The 2025 quarters come from an aggregator.

c8.note: The Q2'26 release states record GAAP operating income of $680M, up $169M year over year.

c9.note: Search results for the Q2'26 release show record net income of $513M with a 7.0% margin. I did not open the cited PDF.

c10.note: Adjusted EBITDA was $769M with a 10.4% margin, down from 12.4%. The dollar amount is a record. The margin is not a record, because it fell year over year.

c11.note: The Q2 2026 release says 2026 guidance is 'an increase from $2.24 billion last year'. I read this in the SEC copy of the release, because the investors.carvana.com PDF returned empty.

c12.note: The Q2 release, dated 2026-07-29, gives FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.7-$3.0 billion, conditional on a stable environment.

c13.note: The 10-Q balance sheet shows cash and cash equivalents of $2,630 million at 2026-06-30. The press-release net debt reconciliation uses the same figure.

c14.note: The 10-Q shows restricted cash of $113 million. It is separate from the $2,630 million of cash, and the two sum to the $2,743 million in the cash flow statement.

c15.note: Note 9 shows gross debt of $5,133 million, before the current portion, issuance costs and premium. The press release's $5,236 million total debt appears to include finance leases (I inferred this, not confirmed), which would explain the gap.

c16.note: A Carvana debt table at 6/30/26 lists finance lease liabilities of $118M. The 10-Q says finance leases sit inside debt, and 5,133 + 118 less about 15 of costs gives the 5,236 balance sheet total. I did not see the figure in the 10-Q lease note itself.

c17.note: The 10-Q balance sheet shows a tax receivable agreement liability of $2,130M at 6/30/26, as a separate line from debt. $1,645M of it is owed to related parties.

c18.note: The 10-Q balance sheet shows total liabilities of $9,414M at 6/30/26, up from $8,998M at 12/31/25.

c19.note: Note 9 shows total debt of $5,133M less a current portion of $319M, excluding finance leases. The balance sheet current-portion line reads $256M, which differs from $319M. Note 9's $319M includes the $126M floor plan line, which the balance sheet shows separately as a revolving facility, so the two are not directly comparable.

c20.note: Note 9 states $32M of 5.500% Senior Unsecured Notes are due April 15, 2027, and this is the entire current portion of the unsecured notes.

c21.note: The Q2 2026 10-Q reports net cash provided by operating activities of $345M for the six months ended 2026-06-30, against $261M a year earlier.

c22.note: The 10-Q liquidity table shows $2,039M of availability under short-term revolving facilities at 2026-06-30. I got this through search results, not by reading the table directly.

c23.note: Committed liquidity was about $4.67B, which equals cash of $2,630M plus revolver availability of $2,039M ($4,669M).

c24.note: Total liquidity resources were $7,024M at 2026-06-30, compared with $6,739M at year-end 2025. The total adds senior secured notes indenture debt capacity and unpledged securities that can be financed.
